title: ADR - Graceful Mesh Health & Deferred Failover Policy
author: Maya Chen
summary: This ADR defines company-wide behavior for detecting degraded mesh health, applying short grace periods to avoid noisy cascading failovers, and performing deferred failover when confirmed. The intent is to preserve warm caches, reduce unnecessary topology changes, and protect SLOs while bounding risk.
context_and_motivation: Redwood runs a multi-tier inference mesh (edge proxies, regional ingress, routing plane, GPU serving pools). Historically, short transient events (GC spikes, network tosses) triggered immediate topology changes that worsened tail latency and invalidated KV caches. Current runbooks treat single-threshold breaches as triggers for topology changes. We need a policy that prefers short mitigation and corroborated signals before topology changes, while still allowing rapid action for safety and security incidents.
principles: 1) Prefer mitigation over topology change to preserve warm runtime state. 2) Require multi-signal confirmation (two independent telemetry planes) before deferred failover. 3) Use short grace windows (30-120s) for soft actions and longer windows (5-15m) for topology changes. 4) Observability-first: every action must be annotated and accompanied by synthetic checks. 5) Safe defaults with operator override: automated policy runs by default; on-call can abort or accelerate with an audited CLI command.
definitions: Soft mitigation: traffic shaping, per-client token bucket limiting, reduced hedging, temporary queue headroom increases (no topology change). Deferred failover: re-routing to alternative candidate pool (regional replica, lower-fidelity pool, or dedicated-hot fallback) which may cause cold starts. Confirmed unhealthy signal: metric crossing threshold plus at least one corroborating signal (e.g., p95 spike + kernel OOM).
signals_considered: API-level: p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, streaming frame drops. Runtime-level: GPU utilization, OOM count, KV eviction surge. Network-level: SYN-RST rate, TCP retransmit %. Synthetic checks: health-check failures from three vantage points. All signals must include dimensions: service, region, model_variant, route, origin_id, correlation_id.
default_thresholds_and_windows: Company baseline examples: p95 inference latency soft >120ms for 30s, confirm window 60s, deferred failover if >120ms sustained for 10m and p99>400ms. 5xx soft >0.4% for 30s, confirm 90s, deferred failover >1.5% for 10m. GPU util soft >92% for 45s, confirm 120s, deferred failover >95% for 10m with OOMs. KV eviction 2x baseline for 30s soft, confirm 120s, deferred failover sustained 3x for 15m.
operational_behavior: Stepwise behavior: 1) Detection: telemetry crosses soft threshold. 2) Soft mitigation (immediate, <=120s): apply per-service traffic shaping (20-40% on non-SLA tiers), pause non-essential background work, increase trace sampling to 100% for affected routes, insert synthetic canary probes. 3) Confirmation: within confirm window, a corroborating signal or synthetic canary failure transitions to monitoring window. 4) Monitoring (5-15m): continue mitigations, notify on-call with suggested runbook steps and deferred failover targets. 5) Deferred failover (manual or automatic by severity): staged reroute with 2% canary for 30s, progressive ramp with holds and rollbacks on SLO regressions, and attempts to preserve identity-bound cached state. 6) Post-failover stabilization: 30m cooldown before further topology changes for same surface.
routing_and_cache_locality: Policy prefers candidate pools that share cache warming artifacts (same rack or region) to minimize cold-start misses. If switching to a lower-fidelity model variant, responses must be annotated with fidelity metadata and enterprise opt-out headers honored. Tenant affinity metadata must be considered; automatic failover will not violate strict per-tenant pool affinity.
telemetry_and_instrumentation_requiremen: All signal pipelines must emit metric name and dimensions (service, region, model_variant, route), origin_id, correlation_id. Actions must be annotated when grace windows start/end, mitigations applied, confirmation decisions, and deferred failover execution. An incident trace must link initial signal to final action for RCA and postmortem analysis. Runbook URL and initiating rule id must be attached to annotations.
runbook_excerpt: On-call summary: 1) Confirm automated mitigations and feature-flag state. 2) Review synthetic canary results and trace samples (links in alert). 3) If deferred failover proposed, evaluate canary target and customer impact. Approve via 'redwoodctl failover approve --service <svc> --target <pool> --reason "oncall-autoproposed" --expires 30m'. 4) Abort automatic plan: 'redwoodctl failover abort --incident <id>'. 5) Roll-forward: follow progressive ramp playbook and monitor p95/p99, error budget, and KV hit-rate.
configuration_matrix: Example YAML snippet for mesh-policy repo: policy_name: graceful-mesh-health-policy version: '1.0' selectors: - service: 'inference-api' region: 'us-west-2' mitigation: soft_shed_pct: 30 trace_sample_rate: 1.0 thresholds: latency_p95_ms: 120 latency_confirm_window_s: 60 error_rate_pct: 0.4 error_confirm_window_s: 90 deferred_failover: candidate_pools: ['us-west-2-replica', 'us-east-1-replica', 'low-fidelity-pool'] confirmation_requirements: 2 monitoring_window_s: 600
testing_and_validation: Unit tests: deterministic policy rule evaluation for synthetic sequences. Integration: simulate transient blips versus sustained degradation to validate that soft mitigation runs and deferred failover is not executed for blips. Chaos: induce edge network tosses and validate cooldowns and canary behaviors. Post-deploy: shadow traffic replay for 24h to validate thresholds on production traffic before enabling automated deferred failover.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (2w): Deploy policy in passive-mode (no automatic deferred failovers) with full telemetry. Stage 2 (2w): Enable automated soft mitigation only; manual approval required for deferred failovers. Stage 3 (4w): Allow automated deferred failover for non-critical tiers behind feature flag; runbook enforced. Stage 4: GA across regions after 12 weeks and successful chaos test.
open_questions_and_decision_rationale: Q: When should a single high-severity signal bypass confirm requirements? A: If signal implies data corruption (checksum failures, signed artifact mismatches) or security incidents, deferred failover can be immediate with operator notification. Q: How to handle enterprise customers requiring strict pool affinity? A: Policy honors per-tenant affinity metadata and falls back to white-listed pools; if none available, notify CS and escalate rather than perform automatic failover.
owner_and_maintenance: Policy steward: Eng Infra - Mesh Reliability team (primary contact: Jonas Keller). Review cadence: quarterly or after any production event involving deferred failover. Related docs: service-dependency-isolation-and-runtime-feature-gating-standards, continuous-fallback-orchestration guide.
appendix_cli_examples: Inspect active grace windows: 'redwoodctl mesh grace list --service inference-api --region us-west-2'. Force-cancel a grace period (oncall only): 'redwoodctl mesh grace cancel --grace-id G12345 --reason "manual-abort"'.
notes: This ADR balances responsiveness to true outages with resilience against noisy transient failures. It prioritizes preserving warm runtime state and improving customer experience during recoveries. Automated actions are auditable and reversible; safety/security signals remain exempt from grace requirements.
